'''Jukka Pekka Pekola''' (born 1958) is a Finnish professor of experimental [[nanophysics]] at [[Aalto University]]. He has worked in the fields of [[low-temperature physics]], [[nanoelectronics]] and [[quantum thermodynamics]]. He is the recipient of the 2020 [[Simon Memorial Prize]].

== Biography ==
Jukka Pekola was born in 1958 in [[Pihlajavesi, Keuruu|Pihlajavesi]], [[Finland]]. He received his M.Sc. (1982) and D.Sc. (1984) degrees from the [[Helsinki University of Technology]]. His doctoral research focused on critical flow and [[persistent current]] experiments in [[superfluid helium-3]]. Both his M.Sc. and D.Sc. work were carried out at the university's Low Temperature Laboratory, founded and led by physicist [[Olli Lounasmaa]]. Pekola continued studying superfluid helium as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="Simon" />

In 1992, Pekola joined the [[University of Jyväskylä]] as part of a new experimental nanophysics initiative launched by {{Ill|Mikko Paalanen (physicist)|lt=Mikko Paalanen|fi|Mikko Paalanen}}. Shifting his research focus from superfluid helium to [[nanoelectronics]], Pekola was instrumental in establishing experimental nanoscience as a research field in Jyväskylä. When Paalanen left in 1995 to become the director of the Low Temperature Laboratory at Helsinki, Pekola was appointed to a professorship in nanotechnology in 1997. Pekola played a role in establishing the interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center in Jyväskylä.<ref name="NSC">{{cite book |url=https://jyx.jyu.fi/jyx/Record/jyx_123456789_44716 |title=Pienestä syntyi suurta / Nano came to Jyväskylä |publisher=University of Jyväskylä |year=2014 |isbn=978-951-39-5911-1 |editor=Heikkilä, Mari |language=fi, en}}</ref><ref name="Ehrnrooth" />

In 2002, Jukka Pekola was appointed professor of quantum nanophysics at the Helsinki University of Technology (later part of [[Aalto University]]), where he founded the PICO research group within the Low Temperature Laboratory. The [[Academy of Finland]] has twice named him an Academy Professor, recognizing his work with a first term in 2000–2005 and a second term in 2014{{Endash}}2018.<ref name="Ehrnrooth" />

In addition to his research activities, Pekola has held roles within Finland's scientific community. He has served as the director of the Academy of Finland's Centre of Excellence in Quantum Technology and as the scientific director of OtaNano, the national research infrastructure for micro- and nanotechnologies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OtaNano |url=https://www.aalto.fi/en/otanano |website=Aalto University |access-date=2025-07-03 |language=en}}</ref> Pekola also directs InstituteQ, a national quantum institute formed by Aalto University, the [[University of Helsinki]], and [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-27 |title=InstituteQ |url=https://instituteq.fi/ |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=InstituteQ |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Ehrnrooth" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-18 |title=Jukka Pekola announced as acting director of InstituteQ |url=https://www.aalto.fi/en/news/jukka-pekola-announced-as-acting-director-of-instituteq |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=Aalto University}}</ref>

Since 2010, he has served as [[Editor-in-chief|Editor-in-Chief]] of the ''[[Journal of Low Temperature Physics]]''.<ref name="JLTP">{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/10909/editors |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Journal of Low Temperature Physics |publisher=Springer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Leiderer |first=Paul |last2=Pekola |first2=Jukka |last3=Sullivan |first3=Neil |date=2019-11-27 |title=Special Issue: 50 Years of the Journal of Low Temperature Physics |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10909-019-02235-1 |journal=Journal of Low Temperature Physics |language=en |volume=197 |issue=3-4 |pages=111–112 |doi=10.1007/s10909-019-02235-1 |issn=0022-2291}}</ref>

== Research ==
Pekola's research explores how heat and energy behave in very small and cold systems—down to the scale of individual electrons and near absolute zero temperature.

In 1994, Pekola and his collaborators introduced the [[Coulomb blockade thermometer]], a type of [[primary thermometer]] that can measure the temperature of electrons at extremely low temperatures without the need for external calibration.<ref name="f984">{{cite journal |last=Pekola |first=J. P. |last2=Hirvi |first2=K. P. |last3=Kauppinen |first3=J. P. |last4=Paalanen |first4=M. A. |date=1994-11-21 |title=Thermometry by Arrays of Tunnel Junctions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.2903 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=73 |issue=21 |pages=2903–2906 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.2903 |issn=0031-9007 |access-date=2025-07-03|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Pekola has also contributed to the development of electronic cooling techniques based on [[tunnel junctions]] between [[superconducting]] and normal metals.<ref name="d990">{{cite journal |last=Leivo |first=M. M. |last2=Pekola |first2=J. P. |last3=Averin |first3=D. V. |date=1996-04-01 |title=Efficient Peltier refrigeration by a pair of normal metal/insulator/superconductor junctions |url=http://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/9511127 |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=68 |issue=14 |pages=1996–1998 |doi=10.1063/1.115651 |issn=0003-6951 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free|arxiv=cond-mat/9511127 }}</ref><ref name="k840">{{cite journal |last=Giazotto |first=Francesco |last2=Heikkilä |first2=Tero T. |last3=Luukanen |first3=Arttu |last4=Savin |first4=Alexander M. |last5=Pekola |first5=Jukka P. |date=2006-03-17 |title=Opportunities for mesoscopics in thermometry and refrigeration: Physics and applications |url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0508093 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=78 |issue=1 |pages=217–274 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.78.217 |issn=0034-6861 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free|arxiv=cond-mat/0508093 }}</ref>

In a 2006 experiment, Jukka Pekola's team demonstrated that heat can be transported by photons through a single channel in a superconducting circuit, confirming that the rate of flow is limited by the [[thermal conductance quantum]].<ref name="r139">{{cite journal |last=Meschke |first=Matthias |last2=Guichard |first2=Wiebke |last3=Pekola |first3=Jukka P. |date=2006 |title=Single-mode heat conduction by photons |url=http://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0605678 |journal=Nature |volume=444 |issue=7116 |pages=187–190 |doi=10.1038/nature05276 |issn=0028-0836 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free|arxiv=cond-mat/0605678 }}</ref> A subsequent 2009 experiment applied these principles to achieve electronic refrigeration at a distance, using impedance-matched superconducting leads to cool a metallic island through a single photonic channel.<ref name="z905">{{cite journal |last=Timofeev |first=Andrey V. |last2=Helle |first2=Meri |last3=Meschke |first3=Matthias |last4=Möttönen |first4=Mikko |last5=Pekola |first5=Jukka P. |date=2009-05-18 |title=Electronic Refrigeration at the Quantum Limit |url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/0902.2584 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=102 |issue=20 |page= |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.200801 |issn=0031-9007 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free|arxiv=0902.2584 }}</ref>

In 2014 and 2015, Jukka Pekola's group built two nanoscale versions of [[Maxwell's demon]] thought experiment. Their first version, a [[Szilard engine]], used information about a single electron's location to extract energy from the surrounding environment, effectively converting information into work.<ref name="n904">{{cite journal |last=Koski |first=Jonne V. |last2=Maisi |first2=Ville F. |last3=Pekola |first3=Jukka P. |last4=Averin |first4=Dmitri V. |date=2014-09-23 |title=Experimental realization of a Szilard engine with a single electron |url=https://www.pnas.org/content/pnas/111/38/13786.full.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=111 |issue=38 |pages=13786–13789 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1406966111 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=4183300 |pmid=25201966 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free}}</ref> They then created a more advanced demon, where one circuit automatically measures and cools a second circuit, acting as an information-powered refrigerator.<ref name="n505">{{cite journal |last=Koski |first=J. V. |last2=Kutvonen |first2=A. |last3=Khaymovich |first3=I. M. |last4=Ala-Nissilä |first4=T. |last5=Pekola |first5=J. P. |date=2015-12-30 |title=On-Chip Maxwell’s Demon as an Information-Powered Refrigerator |url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/1507.00530 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=115 |issue=26 |page= |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.260602 |issn=0031-9007 |access-date=2025-07-03 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1507.00530 }}</ref> Both devices physically demonstrate the fundamental link between information and thermodynamics, showing that information can be used to perform work at the nanoscale.<ref name="r503">{{cite journal |last=Koski |first=Jonne V. |last2=Pekola |first2=Jukka P. |date=2016-08-21 |title=Maxwell's demons realized in electronic circuits |journal=Comptes Rendus. Physique |volume=17 |issue=10 |pages=1130–1138 |doi=10.1016/j.crhy.2016.08.011 |issn=1878-1535 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2017, Pekola received a [[ERC Advanced Grant|European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant]] for developing quantum heat engines and refrigerators and for research on quantum thermodynamics.<ref name="ERC">{{cite web |date=2017-04-07 |title=Nearly 5 million euro for pioneering biomimetics and quantum technology research |url=https://www.aalto.fi/en/news/nearly-5-million-euro-for-pioneering-biomimetics-and-quantum-technology-research |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Aalto University}}</ref>

|url=https://www.iop.org/physics-community/special-interest-groups/low-temperature-group/simon-memorial-prize |website=Institute of Physics |access-date=2025-07-02}}</ref><ref name="AaltoSimon">{{cite web |title=Professori Jukka Pekolalle arvostettu Simon Memorial -palkinto |url=https://www.aalto.fi/fi/uutiset/professori-jukka-pekolalle-arvostettu-simon-memorial-palkinto |website=Aalto University palkinto |url=https://scientiarum.fi/fi/professori-theodor-homenin-palkinto/ |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Suomen Tiedeseura |language=fi}}</ref> the [[Finnish Cultural Foundation]] Award in 2024,<ref name="SKR">{{cite web |title=Henkilökuvassa: Jukka Pekola |url=https://skr.fi/tiede-ja-taide/henkilokuvassa-jukka-pekola/ |website=Suomen Kulttuurirahasto |language=fi |access-date=2025-07-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-02-27 |title=Suomen Kulttuurirahaston palkinnot Villu Jaanisoolle, Heini Junkkaalalle ja Jukka Pekolalle |url=https://skr.fi/blog/suomen-kulttuurirahaston-palkinnot-villu-jaanisoolle-heini-junkkaalalle-ja-jukka-pekolalle/ |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Suomen Kulttuurirahasto |language=fi}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Aulanko-Jokirinne |first=Tiina |date=2024-02-27 |title=Jukka Pekolalle Suomen Kulttuurirahaston palkinto – kvantti kiinnostaa tiede- ja scifimaailman ulkopuolellakin |url=https://www.aalto.fi/fi/uutiset/jukka-pekolalle-suomen-kulttuurirahaston-palkinto-kvantti-kiinnostaa-tiede-ja-scifimaailman |website=Aalto University}}</ref> and the [[Magnus Ehrnrooth Foundation Prize|Magnus Ehrnrooth Prize in Physics]] in 2025.<ref name="Ehrnrooth">{{cite web |title=The Magnus Ehrnrooth Prize in Physics to Prof. Jukka Pekola |url=https://magnusehrnroothinsaatio.fi/en/the-magnus-ehrnrooth-prize-in-physics-to-prof-jukka-pekola-and-the-new-prizes-for-best-doctoral-dissertation-awarded/ |publisher=Magnus Ehrnrooth Foundation |access-date=2025-07-02}}</ref>

Pekola is a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]] and the Finnish Academy of Technical Sciences since 2001.<ref name="Simon" /> He received the [[Order of the White Rose of Finland|First Class Medal of the White Rose of Finland]] from the President of Finland in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jukka Pekola / Prizes |url=https://research.aalto.fi/en/persons/jukka-pekola/prizes/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=Aalto University's research portal |language=en}}</ref>
